title: Segmented workload TTL, batching and quantization playbook
body:
Purpose:
This memo captures a pragmatic playbook for tuning batching, prefix/KV caching TTLs, and quantization per workload segment. It pairs a small spreadsheet model (schema below) with recommended default settings and a short canary/AB test plan so engineers can quickly validate cost vs quality/latency tradeoffs.
body_2:
Why segmented tuning?
- One-size-fits-all qcache/batch settings leave money on the table. Different routes/customers have wildly different sequence-length distributions, prefix-reuse, and SLOs.
- Segmentation enables: targeted TTLs (hot prefix cache), different batching profiles (tiny interactive vs bulk-generation), and conservative vs aggressive quantization ramps tied to risk.
- This reduces token cost and GPU hours while preserving customer experience for high-SLO routes.
body_3:
High-level segmentation heuristic (fast to compute):
1) Route-level aggregates from a 24–72h trace: percent_prefix_reuse (fraction of requests matching a cached prefix/hash); median_seq_len; 90th/99th seq_len; request_rate_per_min; p99_latency.
2) Derived buckets:
   - Hot-prefix interactive: prefix_reuse >= 40% AND median_seq_len <= 128 AND p99_latency target <= 200ms
   - Chat-ephemeral: prefix_reuse < 40% AND median_seq_len <= 512, moderate SLO (p99 <= 800ms)
   - Long-batch/generation: median_seq_len > 512 OR large single-request token counts, throughput-first
   - Bulk-embedding: very short seq_len (<64) but high rate, often can use int8 embeddings quantization
3) Add an entropy check: compute prompt-token-uniqueness by hashing prefix windows; if high entropy, deprioritize aggressive caching.
body_4:
Spreadsheet model: required columns (single sheet)
- route_id
- sample_percent (percent of global traffic)
- median_seq_len
- p90_seq_len
- p99_seq_len
- percent_prefix_reuse
- baseline_cost_per_10k_requests (USD)
- baseline_p50_latency
- baseline_p99_latency
- suggested_batch_size
- suggested_cache_ttl_s
- suggested_quantization_profile
- projected_cost_per_10k_requests_after_changes (formula)
- expected_savings_pct (formula)
- quality_risk (Low/Medium/High)
- notes
Formulas (example cells):
- projected_cost = baseline_cost * (1 - savings_from_batching - savings_from_cache - savings_from_quant)
- savings_from_batching ~ min(0.45, 0.08 * log2(suggested_batch_size)) (calibrated placeholder; replace with measured speedup)
- savings_from_cache = percent_prefix_reuse * (cache_hit_token_fraction) * cache_effectiveness_factor
- savings_from_quant = table_lookup(quantization_profile -> expected_token_cost_reduction)
Note: capture the constants in a small config table so the sheet is editable per-model/hardware.
body_5:
Preset recommendations (starter defaults)
- Hot-prefix interactive:
  - batch size: 4 (prefer latency-preserving micro-batches with async coalescing)
  - cache TTL: 30s–120s depending on prefix churn (start at 45s)
  - quantization: conservative (4-bit qweight for Llama-family or int8 dynamic for exported fp16) applied to head-only weight quantization if quality tests pass
  - expected savings: 20–35%
  - risk: Low/Medium (test on 5 eval prompts)
- Chat-ephemeral:
  - batch size: 8–16 (prioritize throughput when p99 SLO > 400ms)
  - cache TTL: 10s–60s (prefix caching for conversation turns only)
  - quantization: 4-bit mixed (start with 4/8 hybrid)
  - expected savings: 25–45%
  - risk: Medium (run generation quality checks)
- Long-generation/batch:
  - batch size: 32–128 (maximize device utilization)
  - cache TTL: 0–10s (limited benefit for unique long prompts)
  - quantization: aggressive (int8 or 4-bit-wide if model validated for long contexts)
  - expected savings: 35–60% depending on throughput profile
  - risk: Medium/High (watch long-tail quality regressions)
- Embeddings/bulk inference:
  - batch size: 256–1024 (vectorized embedding matrices)
  - cache TTL: 300s–3600s for identical inputs (embeddings are highly cacheable)
  - quantization: int8 embedding kernels or FP16 with product-quantization fallback
  - expected savings: 40–75%
  - risk: Low (validate distance metrics on a holdout)
body_6:
Quantization notes and guardrails
- Maintain a per-model quality baseline (BLEU/perplexity or downstream metric) and require automated regression < 1–2% on critical metrics before wide rollout.
- Two-stage rollout: offline calibration -> canary (1–5% traffic) -> staged ramp (5/20/50/100).
- Keep a fast fallback to FP16/FP32 model variant when regressions detected.
- Use mixed precision: keep attention/key/value accumulators in FP16 where possible and quantize feed-forward weights more aggressively.
- For new model families, run a short AB on n=1000 representative prompts; collect both automated quality signals and a human spot check of 20 prompts.
body_7:
Cache key scheme and TTL ladder
- Key composition: route_id + prefix_hash(first 128 tokens) + model_variant + tenant_id(optional).
- Cache entries store: logits_kv + last_used_ts + hit_count. Eviction: LRU with hot-tier pin for entries with hit_count > 10 in past 5m.
- TTL ladder (suggested defaults):
  - cold-tier: 5–15s (low reuse routes)
  - warm-tier: 30–120s (chat-turn reuse)
  - hot-tier: 300–3600s (embeddings or repeated templates)
- Instrumentation: record per-entry hit_rate, hit_token_fraction (tokens saved when hit), avg_response_delta (latency change when hit vs miss). Use these to recompute TTL weekly.
body_8:
Canary/AB test plan (pragmatic)
- Goal: validate cost reduction without harming p99 latency or downstream quality.
- Canary parameters: 1) create mirroring variant implementing batching/ttl/qconfig; 2) route selection: stratified sampling across segments with minimum traffic floor; 3) start at 5% traffic for 48 hours.
- Metrics to collect (per-route and aggregated):
  - cost_per_10k_requests (realized)
  - p50/p90/p99 latency
  - error_rate and OOM/serve-failures
  - cache_hit_rate and avg_tokens_saved_per_hit
  - automated quality metric (e.g., embedding cosine delta, perplexity delta, or task-score)
  - qualitative sample set: 50 human-checked outputs from high-value routes
- Success criteria: 
  - cost reduction >= 15% on that route OR absolute cost_per_token moves toward target
  - p99 latency not regressed by > 10% (or within agreed SLO slack)
  - quality metric change <= agreed tolerance (typically < 2%)
  - no increase in error_rate
- Rollback: immediate rollback threshold: any sustained p99 degradation > 30% OR error_rate doubling.
body_9:
Operational checklist for onboarding a route to segmented tuning
1) Pull 72h raw traces and compute segmentation metrics.
2) Populate spreadsheet row per route and simulate projected savings.
3) Run offline simulation using sampled traces with a micro-batching emulator to estimate real latency/cost tradeoffs.
4) Run canary for 48–72h with close monitoring.
5) If canary passes, ramp 20% -> 50% -> 100% across 24–72h windows.
6) Schedule a post-mortem measurement 7 days after 100% rollout to confirm sustained savings and surface any regressions.
body_10:
Quick calibration tasks (to get numbers into the sheet)
- Job A: per-model microbench: feed synthetic prompts at target seq_len percentiles and measure tokens/sec across batch sizes [1,2,4,8,16,32,64]. Output as CSV to import.
- Job B: prefix reuse sampler: hash first N tokens across 72h to compute per-route prefix reuse.
- Job C: quantization quality sweep: run 1k eval prompts across qconfigs (fp16, int8, 4-bit, 4/8-hybrid) and capture chosen automated metric.
- Job D: cache simulation: replay traces with an LRU cache sim to compute tokens_saved_by_cache, entry_lifetime distribution, and hit_rate by TTL.
body_11:
Open questions / items for follow-up
- We need a short canonical evaluator per vertical (search, chat, summarization, embeddings). Product should own threshold definitions for quality regressions.
- Should we expose a per-tenant UI in Console that suggests a preset and an expected savings band? (Product + Console team)
- Investigate hardware-aware quantization presets (A100 vs H100 vs AWS chips) and map expected speedups.
- Consider a lightweight inference-simulation package that runs on sampled traces and outputs a scenario comparison (baseline vs configs).

Notes: This is a living document — tweak TTL ladders and batch-size formula coefficients after the first two pilot routes. Add the CSV outputs from calibration jobs into the spreadsheet and pin constants for reproducibility.
